parsed.paper_uuid: Gary Habermas - Chapter 008 - The Evidential THRESHOLD for Resurrection Belief - Gary Habermas

source_selection.exact_source_expression: I do not have a certain threshold that they have to have to meet. ... At no point do I ever say I need this many evidences.
source_selection.reason: This is a precise negative claim about the absence of a numerical evidential threshold in Habermas's minimal-facts methodology. It can be modeled as a statement about a decision procedure that does not depend on a scalar threshold.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A historical-claim evaluation procedure P is threshold-free if there exists no numerical threshold t in the unit interval such that for every claim c, P accepts c iff the evidential score of c is at least t.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: def ThresholdFree (P : HistoricalClaim → Bool) (score : HistoricalClaim → ℝ) : Prop := ¬ ∃ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t ∧ t ≤ 1 ∧ ∀ c, P c = true ↔ score c ≥ t

symbol_table.reader_meaning: A proposition about a past event, e.g. 'the tomb was empty' or 'the disciples had experiences they took to be appearances of the risen Jesus'.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: The 'facts' discussed in the minimal-facts method.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: A numerical evidential score assigned to a historical claim.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: The 'percentage' or 'probability' that Habermas refuses to fix.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: A decision procedure that accepts or rejects a historical claim as believable.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: Habermas's actual practice of accepting minimal facts.

symbol_table.formal_definition: ¬ ∃ t, 0 ≤ t ∧ t ≤ 1 ∧ ∀ c, P c = true ↔ score c ≥ t
symbol_table.reader_meaning: The procedure does not reduce to a single numerical cutoff.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A01: 'I do not have a certain threshold that they have to have to meet.'

explicit_premises: Historical claims can be assigned real-valued evidential scores.
The decision procedure P is a total function from claims to Bool.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one historical claim and at least one score function for the definition to be non-vacuous.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus was not searched; no compilation attempted.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal definition of threshold-free evaluation is proposed.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether Habermas's actual procedure satisfies this definition; whether the score function is well-defined; whether the definition captures the intended meaning.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The definition captures the negative claim that no single numerical cutoff is used. It does not capture the positive claim that categories of evidence (multiple attestation, eyewitness, early sources) are used instead.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Connects to A03 and A04, which describe the positive alternative to a numerical threshold.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: That's by far the more important of the two. Way more. ... number one would be 90 or 85% of the game.
source_selection.reason: This is a comparative claim about the relative importance of two criteria. It can be modeled as a weighted decision rule where the weight on high evidence is much greater than the weight on scholarly consensus.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A two-criterion evaluation procedure assigns weight w1 to high evidence and w2 to scholarly consensus, with w1 > w2 and w1 / (w1 + w2) at least 0.85.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: def TwoCriterionWeight (w1 w2 : ℝ) : Prop := 0 ≤ w2 ∧ w2 < w1 ∧ w1 / (w1 + w2) ≥ 0.85

symbol_table.reader_meaning: Weight assigned to the high-evidence criterion.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: Criterion 1: the fact is highly evidenced.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: Weight assigned to the scholarly-consensus criterion.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: Criterion 2: the vast majority of qualified scholars concur.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: High evidence is at least 85% of the total weight.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A03: 'number one would be 90 or 85% of the game.'

explicit_premises: The two criteria can be assigned real-valued weights.
The weights are non-negative and sum to a positive number.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one pair (w1, w2) satisfying the condition.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus was not searched; no compilation attempted.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal condition for the relative weighting of the two criteria is proposed.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether Habermas's actual procedure satisfies this condition; whether the weights are stable across claims; whether the 85% figure is intended as a precise bound.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The definition captures the comparative claim but not the qualitative reasons for the asymmetry.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Connects to A01 (no numerical threshold) and A02 (consensus percentages not used except for the empty tomb).

source_selection.exact_source_expression: I'd say if I have multiple attestation, eyewitness, and early sources, that's not a list of names, that's a list of categories. And I think those categories to have several of those makes a strong argument.
source_selection.reason: This is a precise claim about the structure of strong evidence: it is a set of categories, and having several of them constitutes a strong argument. It can be modeled as a predicate on sets of evidence categories.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A set of evidence categories S is strong if S contains at least three of the categories {multiple attestation, eyewitness, early sources}.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: def StrongEvidence (S : Finset EvidenceCategory) : Prop := ({EvidenceCategory.multipleAttestation, EvidenceCategory.eyewitness, EvidenceCategory.earlySources} ∩ S).card ≥ 3

symbol_table.formal_definition: inductive EvidenceCategory | multipleAttestation | eyewitness | earlySources | other
symbol_table.reader_meaning: A type of evidence used to support a historical claim.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: The categories Habermas lists: multiple attestation, eyewitness, early sources.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: The set of evidence categories available for a claim.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: The categories Habermas says he has for the minimal facts.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: Having all three named categories makes a strong argument.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A04: 'if I have multiple attestation, eyewitness, and early sources ... those categories to have several of those makes a strong argument.'

explicit_premises: Evidence categories can be represented as a finite set.
The three named categories are distinct.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one set S satisfying StrongEvidence.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus was not searched; no compilation attempted.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal definition of strong evidence as a set of categories is proposed.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the threshold of three categories is intended; whether other categories count; whether the categories are independent.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The definition captures the categorical structure but not the qualitative assessment of each category.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Connects to A01 (no numerical threshold) and A03 (high evidence is more important than consensus).

source_selection.exact_source_expression: I've never counted. Except the empty tomb, and it's not one of the six, I never counted. ... The only time I've done that is the empty tomb.
source_selection.reason: This is a precise claim about the scope of counting: the only claim for which a scholarly consensus percentage was counted is the empty tomb. It can be modeled as a predicate on claims.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A claim c is counted if and only if c is the empty tomb.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: def Counted (c : HistoricalClaim) : Prop := c = HistoricalClaim.emptyTomb

symbol_table.reader_meaning: A proposition about a past event.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: The facts discussed in the minimal-facts method.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: The claim that the tomb of Jesus was empty.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: The empty tomb, the only claim for which Habermas counted scholars.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: A claim is counted only if it is the empty tomb.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A02: 'The only time I've done that is the empty tomb.'

explicit_premises: HistoricalClaim is a type with at least one distinguished element emptyTomb.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one claim (the empty tomb) satisfying Counted.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus was not searched; no compilation attempted.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal definition of the scope of counting is proposed.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the empty tomb is indeed the only counted claim; whether other claims were counted but not reported.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The definition captures the negative claim about scope but not the positive claim that the empty tomb was counted.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Connects to A01 (no numerical threshold) and A03 (consensus is less important).

source_selection.exact_source_expression: If I said, 'Well, Dale, you give uh 51. I'd like at least 80.' They're going to go, 'See, he means 80 for those guys he put that what I mean is they'll either mistake honestly mistake the number or purposely mistake the number and say, 'There you go again. You're telling us what percentage you have to have.'
source_selection.reason: This is a claim about the social consequences of stating a numerical threshold: critics will misrepresent it as a universal requirement. It can be modeled as a game-theoretic or epistemic claim about the effect of publishing a threshold.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: If an author publishes a numerical threshold t for accepting historical claims, then there exists a critic who will assert that the author requires t for all claims, regardless of the author's actual intent.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: conjecture threshold_misrepresentation (t : ℝ) (author : Author) (critic : Critic) : ∃ (c : HistoricalClaim), Misrepresents critic author t c

symbol_table.reader_meaning: A scholar who publishes a threshold.
A person who interprets the author's threshold.
The critic asserts that the author requires the threshold for a particular claim.
symbol_table.source_correspondence: A06: critics mistake the number and say the author is telling us what percentage we have to have.

explicit_premises: Critics can misrepresent an author's threshold.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one author, one critic, and one claim for the conjecture to be non-vacuous.

result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The conjecture captures the claim but is highly abstract and may not be provable without additional assumptions.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Connects to A01 (no numerical threshold) and A02 (consensus percentages not used).
